model_annotations.Bulgarian: This bar chart compares the perplexity of two methods—“Per-Output” (blue bars) and “Per-Layer” (orange bars)—across different sparsity rates ranging from 10% to 80%, with sparsity rates displayed on the horizontal axis in ascending order. The vertical axis represents perplexity on a logarithmic scale, ranging from 10^0 (1) to 10^3 (1000), with major tick marks at 10^1, 10^2, and 10^3, and dashed gridlines at each power of ten. At lower sparsity rates (10% to 50%), both methods exhibit similar, low perplexity values, generally below 10^1, with the Per-Output method slightly lower than Per-Layer in most cases. As sparsity increases to 60%, both methods show a noticeable rise in perplexity, with Per-Output reaching approximately 10^1 and Per-Layer slightly above it. At 70% sparsity, Per-Output perplexity increases to about 10^1.5, while Per-Layer reaches approximately 10^1.7. At 80% sparsity, both methods show a significant jump in perplexity, with Per-Output reaching roughly 10^2.5 and Per-Layer slightly higher, near 10^2.7. The bars are grouped by sparsity rate, with each group containing two adjacent bars representing the two methods, and no visual emphasis or annotations are applied to any specific bar.

The bars are grouped by sparsity rate, with each group containing two adjacent bars for the two methods, and no visual emphasis or annotations are applied to any specific bar.
